cover letter
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent industry experience in marketing or related field.
Experience designing flyers, packages, downloadables, digital ads, and other marketing collateral, using software such as Canva, Figma, applications in the Adobe Creative Cloud, and/or other tools.
Experience creating and/or editing short videos and other media for marketing purposes.
Experience with newsletter marketing, including building newsletter journeys and audience segmentation, using MailChimp or similar platforms.
Experience using social media platforms—such as LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky, and others—to build community, grow audience, and drive engagement.
Experience using online analytics tools to drive the design and execution of marketing campaigns.
Experience selling or supporting professional development programs at the district or school leadership level.

We are seeking a part-time (50%) Education Marketing Specialist to support our mission of building kinder, happier schools and classrooms where everyone belongs. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in mission-driven marketing, metrics, content creation, and cross-functional collaboration.

Design and execute promotional campaigns (email, social, paid) to drive registration for Greater Good Education (GGE) communities of practice and other education programs, in coordination with the Director of Education Partnerships and the Communications Specialist.

The primary responsibility of the Education Marketing Specialist is to develop and execute marketing strategies to promote Greater Good Education’s (GGE) various offerings, especially to meet registration and engagement goals in GGE’s professional learning programs, such as our communities of practice.
Monitor enrollment and engagement data across marketing campaigns to inform updates to the marketing plan and to provide summaries for reports to funders.

The Education Marketing Specialist will focus on strategizing, designing, and packaging multimedia marketing content for outreach to PreK-12 schools and districts, educational organizations, ministries of education, and beyond, and on analyzing the impact of GGE marketing campaigns. Their work will help connect schools with the GGE’s evidence-based resources and create meaningful pathways for educators, schools, and districts to enroll in or adopt GGE programs. Under the supervision and guidance of the Education Director, this position will collaborate closely with the education team to grow and sustain enrollment numbers in Greater Good Education communities of practice, grow new GGE initiatives, increase overall engagement with GGE, draw on data from marketing campaigns to inform GGE’s overall marketing plan, and make a lasting impact on the well-being of school communities.
Build and manage a quarterly registration-focused marketing funnel for Greater Good Education communities of practice.
Create sales materials—one-pagers, program overviews, pitch decks—that the Director of Education Partnerships can use in district and partner conversations.

Create and manage branding and creative for education program offerings and collateral, aligning with GGSC brand guidelines and working with the GGSC’s marketing team, designers, copywriters, and consultants as needed.

Promote new Greater Good Education (GGE) articles and practices, and repurpose existing content — videos, articles, and other materials — into new formats (e.g., clips, social posts, newsletter features, blog posts) to extend the program’s reach and maximize its impact across channels. (As time allows)
Support strategy for GGE newsletters, social media channels, and advertising campaigns, using metrics to inform testing and growth. (As time allows)
Strong background in managing multi-channel digital marketing campaigns, ideally within nonprofit, mission-driven, or cause-based organizations.
A strong understanding of the education ecosystem in the U.S. and abroad, including schools, districts, and national and international educational organizations.
Deep interest in supporting the well-being of education professionals, students, and school communities.
Familiarity with funding sources (state, regional, federal, or international) for professional development for education professionals.
Demonstrated alignment with the Greater Good Science Center’s
Exceptional writing skills.
Strong understanding of the marketing funnel, with demonstrated ability to drive conversions.
Strong collaboration and communication skills.
